findings.finding: In asincrono mode each thread releases its pins at the start of the next MoE node; the later nodes re-acquire the same slices as hits. A deferred wait must keep the pins of in-flight slices across the layer's nodes (released at the next layer's first node), as the retention-policy path already does for follow-up nodes; otherwise an in-flight slice could be evicted while its DMA is running.

anchors: argine: ARGINE_RETENTION_POLICY richiede ARGINE_EXPERT_READ=blocco
findings.finding: A retention policy (b_selected / predicted_protect) forces the blocco read mode with one shard and one ensure_many call from thread 0. Research 3 measured its baseline at about 527 ms/token at 1.5 GiB, whereas the default asincrono LRU path was measured at about 258 ms/token at 1.5 GiB in Research 1 (EXP-025). The two figures come from different builds, sessions and workloads and are NOT a paired comparison; they only establish that the asincrono LRU path is the strongest documented baseline and the one R5 must use.

overlap_opportunities.does_not_exist_causally: Across layers: the experts of layer L+1 are unknown until its router runs; issuing them earlier is prediction (Research 2-4 territory) and is excluded.
overlap_opportunities.exists_causal: Within a layer: after the router decision, the reads of the kinds consumed by the second and third expert node can stay in flight while the first (and second) node compute.
overlap_opportunities.not_hideable: Page commit/zeroing on issue, the first node's own reads, and synchronisation barriers.
